record.paper_title: FPT Suspects and Tough Customers: Open Problems of Downey and Fellows
record.original_question: Given a graph G, an integer S, and an edge-weight function w: E(G) → Z, is there a tour through at least k vertices of G whose total cost is at most S?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following parameterized decision problem.

Input: A finite (undirected) graph G, an integer S, and an edge-weight function w: E(G) → ℤ.
Parameter: A positive integer k.
Question: Does G contain a tour (a closed walk) that visits at least k distinct vertices of G and whose total cost — the sum of w(e) over the edges traversed, counted with multiplicity — is at most S?

Determine whether this problem is fixed-parameter tractable with respect to the parameter k; that is, decide whether it admits an algorithm running in time f(k)·|G|^{O(1)} for some computable function f, or show that it is hard for some level of the W-hierarchy (and therefore unlikely to be FPT).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem (visiting at least k vertices by a tour of total weight at most S, parameterized by k) is known to be fixed-parameter tractable. It reduces to a weighted variant of the k-Path / k-Cycle problem, for which FPT algorithms via color-coding and related algebraic techniques (Alon–Yuster–Zwick and successors) are well established. The annotated open-problems update of Fomin and Marx on Downey–Fellows lists Short Cheap Tour among the questions that have since been resolved positively (FPT).

status_evidence.title: FPT suspects and tough customers: Open problems of Downey and Fellows
status_evidence.snippet: Update on the status of open problems from Downey and Fellows' book Parameterized Complexity, including the Short Cheap Tour problem.
status_evidence.claim: Provides updated status (resolved as FPT) for the Short Cheap Tour problem among Downey–Fellows open problems.

status_evidence.title: Parameterized Approximation Algorithms for TSP
status_evidence.snippet: FPT algorithms for variants of TSP parameterized by the number of vertices visited.
status_evidence.claim: Tour-through-k-vertices style problems admit FPT algorithms via color-coding-like techniques.
